questions.q_en:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The antique clock, which has been in our family for generations, need urgent repairs by a skilled horologist.
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the segment "for generations, need". The subject of the main clause is "The antique clock". The phrase "which has been in our family for generations" is a relative clause describing the clock. "Clock" is a singular noun. Therefore, it requires a singular verb. The verb "need" is in its plural form (or base form used with plural subjects and I/you). The singular form for a third-person singular subject in the present tense is "needs".

Correct sentence: The antique clock, which has been in our family for generations, needs urgent repairs by a skilled horologist.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

· A restrictive relative clause (also known as a defining relative clause) gives essential information about a noun that comes before it: without this clause the sentence wouldn't make much sense. A restrictive relative clause can be introduced by that, which, whose, who, or whom. Comma is not used before a restrictive clause.

A non-restrictive relative clause (also called a non-defining relative clause) provides extra information that could be left out without affecting the meaning or structure of the sentence. Non-restrictive relative clauses are normally introduced by which, whose, who, or whom, but never by that. Comma is used before a non-restrictive clause.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Me and my colleague have decided / to take up the challenging new project / offered by the senior management team.
options_en: Me and my colleague have decided
to take up the challenging new project
offered by the senior management team
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "Me and my colleague have decided". When a pronoun is part of a compound subject (performing the action of the verb "have decided"), the subjective case of the pronoun should be used. "Me" is an objective pronoun. The correct subjective pronoun is "I". Also, it is conventional to place the pronoun "I" after other nouns or pronouns in a compound subject.

Correct Sentence: My colleague and I have decided to take up the challenging new project offered by the senior management team.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Subjective Pronouns: The pronouns I, you, we, he, she, it, and they are known as subjective pronouns because they act as the subjects of verbs: We went to the party. "I" is the correct subjective pronoun here.

· Objective Pronouns: The pronouns me, you, us, him, her, it, and them are called objective pronouns because they act as the objects of verbs and prepositions. "Me" is incorrectly used as a subject.

questions.q_en:
Which of the following words has a similar meaning to the underlined word?

The new evidence presented in court was sufficient to completely exonerate the man of all charges.
questions.solution_en:
Exonerate - refers to officially absolving someone from blame for a fault or wrongdoing.

a) Acquit - This means to free someone from a criminal charge by a verdict of not guilty. This is the correct legal synonym for "exonerate."

b) Exile - This means to expel and bar someone from their native country. It is a form of punishment, not freedom from blame.

c) Condemn - This means to express complete disapproval of, or to sentence someone to a particular punishment. It is an antonym of "exonerate".

d) Examine - This means to inspect someone or something in detail. It is the process that might lead to exoneration, but not the act itself.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

Directions :Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

We sit in the last row, bumped about but free of stares. The bus rolls out of the dull cross roads of the city, and we are soon in the open country side, with fields of sunflowers as far as the eye can see, their heads all facing us. Where there is no water, the land reverts to the desert. While still on level ground, we see in the distance the tall range of the Mount Bogda, abrupt like a shining prism laid horizontally on the desert surface. It is over 5,000 metres high, and the peaks are under permanent snow, in powerful contrast to the flat desert all around. Heaven lake lies part of the way up this range, about 2,000 metres above sea level, at the foot of one of the highest snow-peaks.

As the bus climbs, the sky, brilliant before, grows overcast. I have brought nothing warm to wear. It is all down at the hotel in Urumqi. Rain begins to fall. The man behind me is eating over poweringly smelly goat's cheese. The bus window leaks inhospitably but reveals a beautiful view. We have passed quickly from the desert through arable land to pasture and the ground is now green with grass, the slopes dark with pine. A few cattle drink at a clear stream flowing past moss-covered stones; it is a Constable landscape. The stream changes into a white torrent, and as we climb higher. I wish more and more that I had brought with me something warmer than the pair of shorts that have served me so well in the desert. The stream (which, we are told, rises in Heaven Lake) disappears, and we continue our slow ascent. About noon, we arrive at Heaven Lake, and look for a place to stay at the foot, which is the resort area. We get a room in a small cottage, and I am happy to note that there are thick quilts on the bed.

Standing outside the cottage, we survey our surroundings. Heaven Lake is long, sardine-shaped and fed by snowmelt from a stream at its head. The lake is an intense blue, surrounded on all sides by green mountain walls, dotted with distant sheep. At the head of the lake, beyond the delta of the inflowing stream, is a massive snow-capped peak which dominates the vista; it is part of a series of peaks that culminate, a little out of view, in Mount Bogda itself.

For those who live in the resort, there is a small mess-hall by the shore. We eat here sometimes, and sometimes buy food from the vendors outside, who sell kabab and naan until the last buses leave. The kababs, cooked on skewers over charcoal braziers, are particularly good; highly spiced and well-done. Horse's milk is available too from the local Kazakh herdsmen, but I decline this. I am so affected by the cold that Mr.Cao, the relaxed young man who runs the mess, lends me a spare pair of trousers, several sizes too large but more than comfortable. Once I am warm again, I feel a pre-dinner spurt of energy - dinner will belong incoming - and I ask him whether the lake is good for swimming in.

What is the protagonist wearing in the bus?

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A) The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by all United Nations Member States in 2015 to end poverty, reduce inequality and build more peaceful, prosperous societies by 2030.

B) The SDGs cannot be achieved without the realisation of child rights.

C) Also known as the Global Goals, the SDGs are a call to action to create a world where no one is left behind.

D) As world leaders work to deliver on the 2030 promise, children around the globe are standing up to secure their right to good health, quality education, a clean planet and more.
questions.solution_en:
Sentence A comes first as it introduces the subject of the passage - 'sustainable development goals' and discusses its purposes. Sentence C should come next as it elaborates on their purpose. Sentences B and D form the pair BD as B starts the discussion of SDGs with respect to children, and D carries forward the discussion and mentions what all children around the globe are doing.

So, the correct order is ACBD.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en: Select the correct sentence in passive voice from the following options.
options_en: The marketing team has been preparing the presentation.
The marketing team would prepare the presentation.
The marketing team was preparing the presentation.
The presentation was prepared by the marketing team.
questions.solution_en:
In passive voice, the subject of the sentence receives the action rather than performing it. Option (d) is in passive voice because it emphasizes that the presentation (the subject) received the action (being prepared) by the marketing team. The marketing team is not the subject here; instead, they are the ones doing the action, which is preparing the presentation.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The rest of the options are in the active voice. In these options, the emphasis is on the doer of the action ('the marketing team').

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

No effort has been made by the Indian cricket team to cash off on its vibrant image in the World Cup.
questions.solution_en:
The only meaningful phrasal verbs with the word 'cash' are 'to cash in' and 'to cash up'.

So, options c) and d) are incorrect.

When cashiers and storekeepers cash up, they add up all the money taken from customers during a shift, or at the end of the working day. This phrasal verb does not fit in the given sentence which discusses that the cricket team had made no efforts towards a certain thing in World Cup.

'To cash in on' means 'to get money or another advantage from an event or situation, often in an unfair way'.

The phrase gives the meaning that the Indian cricket team did not unfairly use its vibrant image to get any advantage in the World Cup. It forms a meaningful sentence.

Hence, option a) is correct.

Note: Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) says these antibiotic-resistant "superbug infections" pose a major "global threat" to public health. Such resistance directly caused 1.27 million deaths worldwide in 2019, according to The Lancet, a medical journal. The toll is projected to rise to 10 million deaths per year by 2050, says the WHO. Antibiotics - which are considered to be the first line of defence against severe infections - did not work in most of these cases. India has the highest rate of human antibiotic use in the world. Antibiotic-resistant neonatal infections alone are responsible for the deaths of nearly 60,000 newborns each year. Researchers say the use of antibiotics was exacerbated during the Covid-19 pandemic. The weeks-long Kumbh Mela occurs in four Indian cities. The pilgrims take a holy dip in the river waters on the banks of the cities where the festival is held. The US-based researchers gathered data from some 70,000 patients who turned up at more than 40 clinics at two editions of the festival in 2013 and 2015 held in the cities of Prayagraj - also known as Allahabad - and Nashik.

More than 100 million pilgrims attended the two festivals. In Prayagraj in 2013, the patients had a median age of 46 years and most of them were men. Their common symptoms included fever, cough, runny nose, muscle pain, and diarrhoea. Researchers found that more than a third of patients at the clinics were prescribed antibiotics. In Prayagraj, nearly 69% of the patients reporting upper respiratory tract infections received antibiotics at the free state-run clinics at the festival site. "This is an alarmingly high rate, given that the vast majority of upper respiratory tract infections are viral in nature," the researchers say in a recently published paper. Researchers found that entering a clinic at the Kumbh Mela for any reason carried a one-in-three likelihood of walking out with a prescription for antibiotics. If you sought help for a runny nose, the probability increased to two in three. "When antibiotics were prescribed, there appeared to be little rhyme or reason to guide their selection," the researchers said.

The sentence suggests that information or details were transmitted or conveyed from one person to another. 'Passed down' is the most suitable phrasal verb for this context, as it implies the act of transmitting or handing down information or knowledge from one generation to the next or from one person to another. The other options do not appropriately convey the idea of transferring information from one person to another:

Passed away- typically refers to someone's death.

Passed in-does not convey the intended meaning of transmitting information.

"Passed cut" is not a commonly used phrasal verb and does not convey the intended meaning of transferring information.

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

NOTE:

Phrasal verb: A phrase that consists of a verb with a preposition or adverb or both, the meaning of which is different from the meaning of its separate parts. Example: She has always looked down on me. Here, the phrasal verb 'to look down on someone' doesn't mean that you are looking down from a higher place at someone who is below you; it means that you think that you are better than someone.

questions.q_en: Choose the correct Active/Passive sentence:
options_en: Due to cold weather, the vehicles were by the authorities.
The authorities stopped the vehicles due to cold weather.
The authorities stopped due to the cold weather.
The cold weather stopped due to the authorities.
questions.solution_en:
In an active voice sentence, the following format can be seen 'Subject + Verb (tense may vary) + Object'. For a passive voice sentence, the format is 'Subject (objective case of Active voice) + Verb (based on tense in Active voice) + by + Object (subjective case of the Active voice)'.

Among the given options, the only sentence that appropriately follows the grammatical rules of an Active voice sentence is option (b), 'The authorities stopped the vehicles due to cold weather'.

Options (a), (c) and (d) do not comply with the grammatical requirements of an Active or Passive voice sentence and thus they are negated.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

Active and Passive Voice: When the person doing the action is the subject, the sentence is said to be in active form/voice. When the subject is what the action is directed at, then the sentence is said to be in passive form/voice. For example: Active Voice: Rita and her friends performed a skit. Here 'Rita and her friends' (subject) perform the action. Passive Voice: A skit was performed by Rita and her friends. Here 'skit' is the subject (at which the action is directed).

questions.q_en:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word to fill in the blank.

The positive reviews amplified the restaurant's popularity, while the negative ones __________ its reputation.
questions.solution_en:
Let's look at the meanings of the given options.

Complemented: to make something else seem better or more attractive when combined with it.

Propagated: to produce a new plant using a parent plant.

Tarnished: make or become less valuable or respected.

Propelled: drive or push something forwards.

In this sentence, "amplified" means to increase the effect of something. The antonym for "amplified" is "tarnished", which means to damage or destroy the quality or reputation of something.

So, the sentence becomes: "The positive reviews amplified the restaurant's popularity, while the negative ones tarnished its reputation".

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Passive Voice. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Active Voice.

The enemy settlements were being slowly destroyed by the lieutenant and his army.
options_en: The lieutenant and his army have been slowly destroying the enemy settlements.
The lieutenant and his army were slowly destroying the enemy settlements.
The lieutenant and his army were being slowly destroying the enemy settlements.
The lieutenant and his army was slowly destroying the enemy settlements.
questions.solution_en:
·The correct answer is(b) The lieutenant and his army were slowly destroying the enemy settlements.

·The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into subject of the Active Voice.

·The removal of the helping verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

·The Passive voice in this question is in Past Continuous. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Continuous.

·In Passive voice, the format is: Subject (Objective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Object (Subjective case).

·Thus, the format of Active voice is:Subject + was/were + Verb (ing) + Object.

·For example:

o Math was being practiced by Amit. (Passive Voice)

o Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

·Note: Option (d) is incorrect because the usage of singular verb "was" is incorrect with two subjects "The lieutenant and his army", so plural verb "were" would be the correct usage.

·The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

· Therefore, the correct answer is:The lieutenant and his army were slowly destroying the enemy settlements.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

My friend vanished when the goons came to fight with me.
questions.solution_en:
The underlined word, "vanished," means to disappear suddenly. The sentence implies that the friend left or fled when trouble (goons) arrived. The option that best improves the sentence should maintain this meaning while possibly enhancing clarity or context.

Option a, "mobilised," means to organize or prepare, which doesn't fit.

Option b, "attacked," suggests aggression, which is opposite to fleeing.

Option c, "disappeared when the thugs arrived," maintains the meaning of "vanished" (disappeared) and replaces "goons" with "thugs," a synonym that fits well in formal tone.

Option d, "condemned," means to criticize, which is unrelated.

The revised sentence: My friend disappeared when the thugs arrived to fight with me.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.q_en:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources in order to establish facts and reach new conclusions.
questions.solution_en:
Segmentation- division into separate parts or sections.

Bifurcation- the division of something into two branches or parts.

Research- the systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources in order to establish facts and reach new conclusions.

Announcement- a formal public statement about a fact, occurrence, or intention.

Among the given options, the word that matches the meaning of the given group of words is option (c) 'research'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).
